text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Major oil products marketers say the fuel shortage being experienced in Lagos should ease from Thursday as 34 million litres of petrol arrives from refineries in southeast Nigeria.
- Nigeria plans to review 1995 decree setting up investment promotion council in order to boost inflow of direct foreign investment, finance ministry sources say.

- Official commissioning of Chevron Nigeria's $569 million Escravos gas project next month is to be postponed although production of 165 million cubic metres of gas daily from the facility will commence in the first week of May.
- Government accuses pro-democracy activists of planning to disrupt transition to civil rule programme and says it will deal decisively with any sabotage activities.
- High court judge orders drug agency to free Afrobeat musician Fela Anikulapo-Kuti, who was arrested last week for alleged possession of cannabis.
- Three million shares traded on Nigerian stock exchange as business picks up again after the installation of a new computerised clearing system.
- United Nations commission votes to send a special investigator to probe human rights violations in Nigeria.
- Nigeria Airways sacks its newly-appointed insurance brokers.
